hints: Look closely at the reaction conditions, reflux with excess oxidising agent tells you how far oxidation of a primary alcohol will go.
Start by converting 2.30 g of ethanol, $M_r = 46.0$, into moles to find how many moles of product could form.
Work out the theoretical mass of ethanoic acid, $M_r = 60.0$, from those moles, then take 60.0% of it for the actual collected mass.
walkthrough:
**Identify the organic product**

Ethanol is a primary alcohol. With excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI) and boiling under reflux for one hour, it is fully oxidised past ethanal to ethanoic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2[O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Calculate moles of ethanol used**

Moles tells us how many particles we start with. Use moles equals mass divided by $M_r$.

$$n(\text{ethanol}) = \frac{2.30}{46.0} = 0.0500 \text{ mol}$$

**Find the theoretical mass of ethanoic acid**

The equation is 1:1, so 0.0500 mol of ethanol gives 0.0500 mol of ethanoic acid if yield were 100%. $M_r$ of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is 60.0.

$$m_{theoretical} = 0.0500 \times 60.0 = 3.00 \text{ g}$$

**Apply the percentage yield**

Only 60.0% of the theoretical amount was actually collected by distillation.

$$m_{actual} = \frac{60.0}{100} \times 3.00 = 1.80 \text{ g}$$

options.A: This is the mass if the product were ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$. 0.0500 mol x 44.0 = 2.20 g, then 60% gives 1.32 g. Ethanal forms with distillation and limited oxidant, not with excess oxidant under reflux.
options.B: This simply takes 60% of the starting mass, 2.30 x 0.60 = 1.38 g. It ignores that the $M_r$ changes from 46.0 to 60.0 during oxidation, so moles must be used, not direct mass.
options.C: This is correct. Full oxidation under reflux with excess gives ethanoic acid. Theoretical mass is 3.00 g and 60.0% yield gives 1.80 g collected.
options.D: This is the 100% theoretical yield of ethanoic acid, 0.0500 x 60.0 = 3.00 g. It forgets to multiply by 60.0% for the actual yield.
